topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic sets up the lecture by reviewing previous practical work and outlining the main learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor virology and experimental assays of cellular transformation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how the study of transforming retroviruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for measuring transformed phenotypes.

topics.label: Functional classes and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the main categories of cancer-driving mutations and illustrate how mutations in genes like Rb and p53 alter cell cycle regulation and cellular phenotypes.

topics.label: Mechanisms, pathways, and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the distinction between sequence instability and chromosomal instability, detailing the DNA repair, replication, and mitotic failures that cause them alongside their cellular effects.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how sequential mutation acquisition drives tumorigenesis and how inherited germline mutations accelerate cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture, recommends supplementary reading, and previews the upcoming session.
